Preset Editor Guide

What is Preset Editor?

The Preset Editor is where you create and manage form presets - collections of form field configurations that can automatically fill forms on your pages.

Creating a Preset

  • Select "Create New Preset" from the dropdown
  • Enter a Preset Name and optional Description
  • Click "Add Field" to manually add form fields
  • Or use content script to scan the page for existing fields
  • Click "Save" when done

Field Configuration

Each form field can be configured with:

  • Title: Display name for the field
  • Type: Input type (text, checkbox, radio, dropdown, etc.)
  • Value: The value to fill into the field
  • Test ID: data-testid attribute for precise targeting
  • Selector: CSS selector for finding the element
  • Delay (ms): Wait time before filling the field (useful for dynamic forms)

Pro Tip: Use Test ID when available - it's more reliable than CSS selectors. Many modern web apps use data-testid attributes for testing.

Field Actions

  • Drag & Drop: Click and drag the order column to reorder fields
  • Insert After: Add a new field below the current one
  • Duplicate: Create a copy of the field
  • Delete: Remove the field from the preset
  • Move (Re-order): Use the move action to jump this field to a specific position in the list
  • Share: Click the share icon to copy or share this field's configuration with other presets

Import/Export

  • Export: Save your preset as a JSON file for backup or sharing
  • Import: Load a preset from a JSON file
  • Link to Pages: Associate this preset with multiple page profiles

Keyboard Shortcuts

Ctrl + F - Search for fields in the table

Saved Values Guide

What are Saved Values?

Saved Values are individual form field values that you've saved while filling out forms. They're stored per-page and can be quickly accessed through the Live Assistant popup.

How Saved Values Work

When you're filling out a form on a page:

  • Click on any input field to trigger the Live Assistant popup
  • The popup shows previously saved values for similar fields
  • Click a saved value to instantly fill the field
  • Or save a new value by typing and using the save option

Managing Saved Values

In this tab, you can:

  • View: See all saved values for this page
  • Edit: Modify field labels, values, or selectors
  • Delete: Remove values you no longer need
  • Import/Export: Backup or share your saved values

Pro Tip: Saved Values are perfect for storing frequently-used information like email addresses, phone numbers, or addresses without creating full presets.

Saved Values vs Presets

  • Saved Values: Individual field values, accessed one at a time through Live Assistant
  • Presets: Complete form configurations, applied all at once with a button click

Use Saved Values for quick, ad-hoc filling. Use Presets for repeatedly filling entire forms.

Field Identification

Each saved value stores:

  • Field Label: Human-readable name
  • Value: The actual content to fill
  • Test ID: data-testid for reliable targeting
  • Selector: CSS selector as fallback
  • Last Updated: Timestamp of last modification
